title: Nuevo Laredo Named Transparency Leader as Tamaulipas Congress Flags Other Cities' Spending
excerpt: The Tamaulipas State Congress recognized Nuevo Laredo as a leader in auditing results, accountability and transparency over the last five years, while warning other municipalities to clear up their public accounts.
content:
The Tamaulipas State Congress has recognized Nuevo Laredo as a leader in auditing results, accountability and transparency over the last five years, in an evaluation that contrasts sharply with other municipalities in the state facing audits over unfinished works and unproven spending.

Local Deputy Eliphaleth Gómez Lozano, president of the Congress's Board of Directors, recognized the performance of Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, crediting the municipal team's technical capacity and the order in the administration of the public budget.

The lawmaker said several municipalities in the state have accumulated serious questions after the review of their public accounts, with audits finding everything from incomplete files to possible diversions of resources. The deficiencies observed include unfinished works, insufficiently specified payrolls, personal expenses charged to current spending, and a lack of documentation and photographic evidence of the work performed.

Gómez Lozano warned that municipalities with observations have 120 business days from notification to resolve the irregularities. Those that do not comply will see their cases sent to the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Combating Corruption to determine responsibilities.

He stressed that municipal governments must document the use of every peso of the budget, and noted that information about public accounts can be consulted on the Congress's official portal.

Source: Congress of the State of Tamaulipas, Nov. 22, 2026.
